title: Contributor Journey Ops and Benefits Compact
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Purpose

This compact reference consolidates the operational steps, role and career ladder guidance, benefits highlights, and internal tools flow for contributors at Redwood. It is intended for new joiners, hiring managers, and people-ops partners who need a single-page operational playbook for the first 90 days and career mobility touchpoints.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees (FTEs) and long-term contractors with >6 months assignment.
- Supplements team-level onboarding guides and detailed benefit plan documents (links in Related pages).

Quick-start checklist (first 7 days)

1. Complete ID & payroll forms in HR Portal (hr.redwood.internal).
2. Confirm SSO provision: Okta -> Google Workspace -> Slack -> Redwood VPN.
3. Complete Security Awareness training (assigned via LMS).
4. Request project-level repos and Jira boards using Access Request CLI (example below).
5. Schedule 1:1 with manager and onboarding buddy.

Example CLI to request tool access

$ ./scripts/request-access --tool slack --scope "#team-channel" --reason "new hire: product infra"

Role ladder overview (summary)

This section provides the canonical expectations across contributor levels. Use this as a conversation starter for manager calibration. Detailed competency matrices per function live on the Role Framework page.

| Level | Title examples | What success looks like (high level) | Typical time-to-promo range |
|-------|----------------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| L1 | IC1 / Associate | Executes well-scoped tasks, reliable delivery, asks for help early | 12–24 months |
| L2 | IC2 / Contributor | Independently owns features, communicates trade-offs, mentors juniors | 18–30 months |
| L3 | Senior IC | Leads cross-team initiatives, drives design, measurable impact | 24–48 months |
| L4 | Staff / Principal | Shapes product direction, technical leadership, influences org strategy | 36+ months |

Promotion rubric (manager checklist)

- Evidence of sustained impact across at least 3 months.
- Peers and cross-functional collaborators provide supporting examples (use calibration form).
- Demonstrated mastery of role-specific competencies and company leadership behaviors.
- Manager submits promotion packet to People Ops including: summary, evidence, upward feedback, and updated role profile.

Career mobility and rotations

- Lateral moves and 90-day rotations are encouraged when they align with product needs and career goals.
- Request process: discussion with current manager -> written rotation proposal -> receiving manager signs acceptance -> people-ops records the change.
- For critical skills (security, infra, privacy), rotations require a short handover checklist and an appointed mentor.

Benefits and perks (high level)

- Health & wellness: comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans; Health Savings Account (HSA) options.
- Time off: generous vacation policy, paid parental leave (primary and secondary), and flexible personal days.
- Financial: 401(k) with employer match; equity grants on hire and periodic refresh cycles.
- Work environment: hybrid stipend (home office setup), commuter benefits in select regions, learning allowance of $1,200/year.
- Family & caregiving: backup care credits, fertility benefit partner, and paid caregiver leave.

How to navigate benefit questions

1. Check the Benefits Portal (benefits.redwood.internal) for plan details and eligibility windows.
2. Submit a ticket to People Ops (help.redwood.internal) for enrollment exceptions or special cases.

Hybrid work and home office stipend summary

- Eligibility: all full-time contributors after 30 days.
- Stipend: $400 one-time setup + $50/month equipment allowance (USD markets; regional adjustments apply).
- Approved purchases: ergonomic chair, monitor(s), keyboard, and connectivity accessories. Submit receipts to Expense Portal with tag: HOME_OFFICE.

Manager responsibilities during onboarding

- Week 1: set clear 30/60/90 day goals, assign a buddy, and provide team overview.
- Week 2–4: schedule cross-functional intros, ensure required accesses are granted, review first deliverables.
- Ongoing: monthly growth check-ins, career conversations every 6 months.

Internal tools and access flow (abridged)

- Okta (SSO) -> Google Workspace (email & drive) -> Slack -> Jira -> Confluence -> Internal CI & Deploy portals.
- Access request paths: self-serve where available (Access Catalog) or manager-request via Access Request CLI.

Sample access matrix (roles -> tools)

| Role bucket | Minimum access day 1 | Notes |
|-------------|----------------------|-------|
| Engineering | GitHub readonly, Jira write, Slack | Repo write after code review + manager approval |
| Product | Jira, Confluence, Analytics dashboard | Data access require signed NDA for PII datasets |
| Sales | CRM, Confluence, Slack | Customer data access gated by NDAs and training |

Onboarding timeline: 0–90 days (recommended cadence)

- Day 0–1: Paperwork, SSO, hardware.
- Week 1: Team intro, first 1:1, micro-deliverable assigned.
- Week 2–4: Complete security & compliance trainings, contribute to an internal doc or minor bug.
- Month 1: 30-day check-in (manager).
- Month 2: Cross-team project pairing, first performance feedback cycle prep.
- Month 3: 90-day review; calibrate goals and discuss career path.

Learning and mentorship programs

- Buddy program: 12-week pairing for new contributors. Sign-up happens automatically during onboarding.
- Learning stipend: submit receipts and a short one-paragraph learning plan to Learning Ops.
- Internal workshops: weekly brown-bag schedule posted in #learning.

Leaving and offboarding (key operational steps)

1. Manager initiates offboarding ticket (People Ops) with last day and transfer plan.
2. Revoke access timeline: critical systems removed on last day EOD; archival of email and drive following policy.
3. Knowledge transfer document due one week before last day; assign successor reviewer.

Frequently asked questions

Q: Who approves my rotation?
A: Your current manager and the receiving manager. People Ops processes the paperwork.

Q: How fast can I change teams?
A: A typical lateral move takes 3–6 weeks from proposal to first day in the new team (includes approvals and training).
